mainTopic: Fines for deliberate acts in ביטול, and when a person is believed that he ruined something (פיגול, טהרות, a ספר תורה).
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about ערלה nuts that fell into other nuts and broke. The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה fines even an accidental break: otherwise people would break the nuts on purpose and fake an accident. It then sets רבי יוסי against himself, and answers that nobody risks his whole vineyard for one sapling, so that rare case needed no fine. A new משנה teaches that כהנים who make a קרבן פיגול on purpose must pay. A ברייתא follows about when a coworker is believed that he ruined טהרות or זבחים, explained differently by אביי and רבא. רבי אסי says the תורה believes such a person. The proof brought from the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים falls with 'קשיא'. The amud ends with two stories of a סופר who admits a hidden flaw in a ספר תורה he sold. רבי אמי says the סופר loses his pay but the scroll stays valid. רבי אבהו says the סופר's word makes the scroll unusable too.

steps.title: Broken ערלה nuts: accidental versus deliberate
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about ערלה nuts that fell into a mixture and were broken records a disagreement. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say they are never nullified. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say an accidental break allows ביטול but a deliberate break does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the nuts fell into a mixture and broke, whether by accident or on purpose, they are not nullified. This is the view of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: if they broke by accident, they are nullified; if on purpose, they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it just quoted about ערלה nuts mixed with other nuts. This text sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whole פרך nuts are considered important, so they are not nullified in a mixture. Once broken, they lose that importance, which raises the question of whether ביטול now works. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say no even for an accidental break, so they are fining the accidental case. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון fine only the deliberate case.

keyTerms.meaning: done by accident, without intending it

phrases.english: They fell in and were broken;
phrases.notes: This is about ערלה nuts from a place called פרך that fell into other nuts. The ברייתא started just before this.

phrases.english: whether by accident or on purpose,
they are not nullified,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
by accident, they are nullified;
on purpose, they are not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְלוּ וְנִתְפַּצְּעוּ; אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג, וְאֶחָד מֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting just before this section, as the source for a challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה: broken ערלה nuts are never nullified. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: an accidental break allows ביטול, a deliberate one does not.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה fine an accident in a rabbinic matter?
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law, a forbidden item is nullified in a majority. Only the רבנן said important items are not nullified. Yet רבי יהודה fines even the accidental break, which seems to clash with his view that accidents are not fined in rabbinic matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, by Torah law one forbidden item is nullified among two permitted ones, and it was the רבנן who made the decree. Yet רבי יהודה still imposes a fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's position from the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said רבי יהודה does not fine an accidental act when only a rabbinic law is involved. In the nut case, the Torah would allow ביטול by simple majority. The stricter rule for important items is only a rabbinic decree. So refusing ביטול even for an accidental break looks like a fine on a שוגג in a rabbinic matter.

keyTerms.meaning: one is nullified among two, meaning a simple majority cancels it

phrases.english: But here,
where by Torah law one in two is nullified,
and it is the Rabbis who decreed,
and yet Rabbi Yehuda imposes a fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא in step 1 to attack רבי יהודה's earlier stated position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה does not fine a שוגג because of a מזיד in rabbinic laws.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that important items are not nullified is only rabbinic. Even so, רבי יהודה refuses ביטול for an accidental break, which is a fine on a שוגג in a rabbinic matter.

steps.title: The fine prevents people from gaming the system
steps.stepSummary: In the nut case, רבי יהודה fines the accidental break for a special reason. Otherwise people would break nuts on purpose and claim it was an accident in order to get ביטול.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, this is רבי יהודה's reason: because otherwise a person will come to use trickery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The nut case has its own special reason for the fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's general rule still holds: he does not fine accidents in rabbinic laws. The nut case is an exception, because breaking a nut is easy to fake as an accident. Someone wanting ביטול could crack the nuts on purpose and say it just happened.

keyTerms.meaning: to act with trickery or cunning

phrases.english: There, this is Rabbi Yehuda's reason:
because he will come to use trickery.
phrases.notes: He would break the nuts on purpose and pretend it was an accident, just to get them nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special reason for this case: an exception, not a reversal of the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to be fining a שוגג because of a מזיד in a rabbinic matter, against his own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fine in the nut case is a separate safeguard against people faking an accident. רבי יהודה's general rule stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not fine accidents in rabbinic laws. The broken-nut case is an exception, because people could easily fake the accident.

steps.title: רבי יוסי against רבי יוסי: the משנה of mixed saplings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a contradiction within רבי יוסי's views. It quotes a משנה about saplings of ערלה or כלאי הכרם that got mixed with other saplings. The first opinion there allows ביטול in two hundred only if the person did not pick the fruit in order to nullify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction between one statement of רבי יוסי and another, as we learned: a sapling of ערלה or of כלאי הכרם that got mixed with other saplings should not be picked. If he picked it, the forbidden fruit is nullified in two hundred, provided he did not intend to pick for that purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge and quotes the first half of a משנה. This sets up a contradiction that becomes complete in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first opinion follows the same idea as the nut case. Picking with intent to get ביטול is penalized. This half supplies the background for רבי יוסי's dissent, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden mixtures of grapevines with other crops
one in two hundred, the ratio needed for ביטול of ערלה and כלאים

phrases.aramaic: וְרָמֵי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי – דִּתְנַן:
phrases.english: And they set Rabbi Yosei against Rabbi Yosei, as we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת ערלה.

phrases.aramaic: נְטִיעָה שֶׁל עׇרְלָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם
phrases.english: A sapling of orla or of diverse kinds of the vineyard
that became mixed among other saplings,
he should not pick the fruit.
And if he picked, they are nullified in one to two hundred,
provided that he did not intend to pick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבי יוסי's view from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling in step 1 that a deliberate break of the nuts prevents ביטול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: it brings a משנה where רבי יוסי's opinion, quoted next, will clash with that ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוסי allows nullification even when done on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that even someone who picks on purpose gets ביטול in two hundred. That seems to clash with his ruling that deliberately broken nuts are not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even one who intends to pick, the forbidden fruit is nullified in two hundred!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the contradiction. Here רבי יוסי allows ביטול even for a deliberate act, but with the nuts he did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the nuts, רבי יוסי penalized a מזיד by refusing ביטול. With the saplings, he does not penalize a מזיד at all. Both cases involve a deliberate act that brings about ביטול, so his two rulings seem inconsistent. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: one who intends, acting on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a dispute between two different חכמים. The contradiction is between two rulings of the same person, רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
even one who intends to pick,
they are nullified in one to two hundred!
phrases.notes: Compare step 1, where רבי יוסי said nuts broken on purpose are not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמִּתְכַּוֵּין לְלַקֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the contradiction opened in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling in step 1 that deliberately broken nuts are not nullified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the sapling case, רבי יוסי allows ביטול even for a deliberate act. That clashes with his refusal to allow ביטול when the nuts were broken on purpose.

steps.title: Nobody ruins his vineyard for one sapling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רבי יוסי's views. רבא, and also רבי יוחנן (as reported by רבין), say there is a חזקה that a person does not make his whole vineyard forbidden over one sapling. So the deliberate sapling case is rare and was not fined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about that משנה: רבא said, there is a presumption that a person does not make his vineyard forbidden for the sake of one sapling. And when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן the same thing: there is a presumption that a person does not make his vineyard forbidden for the sake of one sapling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Steps 4-5. It explains why רבי יוסי allows ביטול even when someone picks the sapling's fruit on purpose, but does not allow it when nuts are broken on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting a forbidden sapling in a vineyard on purpose would put the whole vineyard at risk, so people simply don't do it. Because this case almost never happens, the רבנן did not make a fine for it. Breaking nuts on purpose is easy and could happen often, so there they did fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it already said about it? An opening that brings an earlier explanation as the answer.
A presumption: what we assume people normally do.
A sapling, a young planted tree

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי fines a deliberate act only when it is something people would actually do. Risking a whole vineyard over one sapling is too rare to need a fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic fine depends on how often the bad behavior would really happen.

phrases.english: Wasn't it already stated about it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the sapling משנה quoted in Step 4, where רבי יוסי lets the fruit be cancelled out even when it was picked on purpose.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There is a presumption that a person does not forbid
his vineyard for the sake of one sapling.
And similarly, when Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is a presumption that a person does not forbid
his vineyard for the sake of one sapling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how common they are: the sapling case is rare, while breaking nuts on purpose is common.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seemed to fine deliberate acts with nuts but not with saplings, which looked inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nobody risks his whole vineyard for one sapling, so that case is rare and was not fined. Deliberately breaking nuts is common, so it was fined.

steps.title: Priests who make an offering פיגול on purpose
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: כהנים who make a קרבן פיגול in the מקדש on purpose must pay for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: כהנים who made a קרבן פיגול in the מקדש, if they did it on purpose, are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה. It teaches that a כהן who ruins a קרבן on purpose by having a wrong intention must pay the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול happens when a כהן thinks, during the service, of eating or offering the קרבן after its proper time. Nothing physical happens to the animal, but the קרבן becomes invalid. The משנה still makes him pay when he did it on purpose, so the owner can bring a new קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined because the כהן had in mind to eat or offer it after its proper time.

steps.confusionAlert: פיגול here is not about the meat itself being bad. The כהן ruined the קרבן only through his thoughts, and he must still pay.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Priests who made an offering piggul in the Temple,
if they did it on purpose, they are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic in the משנה, continuing the chapter's theme of damage that cannot be seen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who deliberately makes a קרבן פיגול must pay the owner.

steps.title: When a coworker is believed that he ruined things
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone working with another person on טהרות or זבחים is believed if he says they became טמא or פיגול. If he says it happened on a certain past day, he is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if one was preparing pure foods with another and said, 'The pure foods I prepared with you became impure,' or was preparing sacrifices with him and said, 'The sacrifices I prepared with you became פיגול,' he is believed. But if he said, 'The pure foods I prepared with you on such-and-such a day became impure,' or 'The sacrifices I prepared with you on such-and-such a day became פיגול,' he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about whether a person is believed when he claims he ruined something he worked on with someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases. In the first, he speaks while still working with the other person, and he is believed. In the second, he talks about something done on a specific day in the past, and he is not believed. The ברייתא gives no reason for the difference, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This opens a ברייתא.
Food prepared in a state of purity.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
If one was preparing pure foods with another,
and he said to him:
The pure foods that I prepared with you became impure;
or he was preparing sacrifices with him,
and he said to him:
The sacrifices that I prepared with you became piggul, he is believed.
But if he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: טְהָרוֹת שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי עִמְּךָ בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי נִטְמְאוּ,
phrases.english: The pure foods that I prepared with you on such-and-such a day became impure,

phrases.aramaic: וּזְבָחִים שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי עִמְּךָ בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי נִתְפַּגְּלוּ –
phrases.english: or the sacrifices that I prepared with you on such-and-such a day became piggul,
he is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ בִּטְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on a related question: is a person believed when he says he caused פיגול or טומאה?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coworker is believed that the items became טמא or פיגול, but not when he says it happened on a specific past day.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the person is believed in the first case of the ברייתא but not in the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first part, and what is different about the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the real difference is between the two halves of the ברייתא. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both halves the person makes the same kind of claim, that the items were ruined. The only visible change is mentioning a specific past day. The גמרא wants the principle that explains why that detail makes him lose his credibility.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching.
The last part of a teaching.

phrases.english: What is different about the first clause,
and what is different about the latter clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the two rulings in the ברייתא of Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains why he is believed in the first case but not in the second.

steps.title: He is believed about what is still in his hands
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: a person is believed about anything that is still in his power to do. While he is still working on the items, he could ruin them now, so he is believed. Once the work is in the past, he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Whatever is still in his power, he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the rule that explains the ברייתא: a person is believed about something he is still able to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he is still working with the טהרות or זבחים, he could make them טמא or פיגול right now, so his claim is believed. Once he talks about a past day, the work is finished and out of his hands, so it is no longer in his power and he is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever is still in his hands, meaning in his power to do.

steps.whatToRemember: כל שבידו נאמן: a person is believed about something he still has the power to do.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is used in many places in הלכה to decide when one person's word is enough.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Whatever is in his power, he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is believed when the matter is still in his power. While he is working, he could still ruin the items; about a past day, he no longer can.

steps.title: רבא's explanation: he stayed quiet at first and spoke up later
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא differently. The person is not believed when he met his partner once and said nothing, then met him again later and said the items were ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where he met him and said nothing at all, and only later met him again and told him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the question of Step 9: why is the person believed in one case of the ברייתא but not in the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the difference is whether it is still in the person's power to ruin the items. רבא says both cases may be about the past. What matters is that in the second case he had a chance to speak earlier and stayed silent, so his later claim looks made up.

keyTerms.meaning: that he found him / met him

phrases.english: Rava said:
For example, where he met him
and did not tell him anything at all,
and afterward he met him again and told him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of Step 9, in place of אביי's answer in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא believes the person in one case and not in the other.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is not believed when he was silent at an earlier meeting and spoke up only later.

steps.title: A story: רבי אמי rules the man is not believed about a past day
steps.stepSummary: A man told his friend that טהרות they made together on a past day had become טמא. רבי אמי ruled that by strict law he is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his friend: The pure items I made with you on such-and-such a day became impure. The friend came before רבי אמי, who said: By the strict rule, he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case that matches the second part of the ברייתא, a claim about a past day, and gives רבי אמי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the claim is about a day that has passed, the man can no longer ruin the items now. רבי אמי follows the simple reading of the ברייתא and says he is not believed. This ruling sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: food or items kept ritually pure
the strict letter of the law

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his friend:
The pure items that I made with you
on such-and-such a day became impure.
He came before Rabbi Ami.
phrases.notes: The one who came is the friend, the owner of the items, asking what to do.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שׁוּרַת הַדִּין אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: By the strict rule, he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that applies the ברייתא's case of a claim about a past day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who says shared טהרות became טמא on a past day is, by strict law, not believed.

steps.title: רבי אסי objects: the Torah believes him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי questions רבי אמי's ruling. He quotes רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי יוסי: the תורה believes such a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said before him: My teacher, you say this? רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי: What can I do, since the תורה believed him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי challenges רבי אמי's ruling with an earlier teaching that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said the man is not believed about the past. רבי אסי quotes רבי יוסי, who says that even though logic might say otherwise, the תורה itself believes such a person. So the ruling seems to go against a known teaching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said before him:
My teacher, you say this?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: So said Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
What can I do, since the Torah believed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אמי's ruling in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's ruling that the man is not believed about a past day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי, quoted by רבי יוחנן, taught that the תורה believes such a person, so ruling that he is not believed goes against that teaching.

steps.title: Where does the Torah believe him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the תורה we see that such a person is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did the Torah believe him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוסי's claim that the תורה believes him. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק says this directly. So the גמרא wants to know which case in the תורה shows that a person is believed about ruining something even after the fact.

phrases.english: Where did it believe him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבי יוסי's teaching in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The place in the תורה that shows such a person is believed.

steps.title: Proof from the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא proves it from the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים. He is believed when he says he made the קרבן פיגול, even though nobody else could have seen what he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא said: The כהן גדול on יום הכפורים proves it. When he says he made it פיגול, he is believed. How else would we know? It is written: 'And no man shall be in the אהל מועד.' So is it not because he is believed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא brings a proof that the תורה believes a person about ruining a קרבן even after the work is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול serves inside alone, and no one else may be there. If he later says he had a wrong thought that made it פיגול, the only way we can know is by believing him. He says this after the service is over, when he can no longer ruin it, and he is still believed.

keyTerms.meaning: a קרבן ruined by a wrong intention during the service
the Tent of Meeting, the holy area

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Bisna said:
The High Priest on Yom Kippur will prove it,
since when he says it was פיגול, he is believed.
And how would we know?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְכׇל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״!
phrases.english: But it is written: 'And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting'!
Rather, is it not because he is believed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14 by bringing a proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's teaching that the תורה believes a person who says something was ruined, even after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The כהן גדול on יום הכפורים, who serves alone (ויקרא 16:17) and is still believed when he says the קרבן was פיגול.

steps.title: Maybe people heard him say it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe we know about the פיגול because people outside heard him say the wrong intention out loud during the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps we heard him make it פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down the proof from the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that the only way to know is to believe him afterward. But maybe he said the wrong intention out loud while serving, and people heard it. Then we would know from hearing him, not from believing his later claim.

phrases.english: But perhaps we heard him make it פיגול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the כהן גדול, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There may be another way to know about the פיגול: people may have heard him say it during the service.

steps.title: Even if we heard him, we still need to believe him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the proof. Even if we heard him, if he were not believed we could think he said it only after the service was done. So he must be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he were not believed, then even if we heard him he would still not be believed, because perhaps he said it only afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push-back of Step 16, and the proof from the כהן גדול stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People outside cannot tell exactly when he spoke. Maybe he said the words after the blood was already sprinkled, when it was too late to ruin the קרבן. So hearing him does not help unless we believe him about when he thought it, and that shows the תורה believes him.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a person is believed about ruining something while it is still in his power. According to רבא, he is believed unless he stayed quiet at an earlier meeting and spoke up only later. רבי יוסי adds that the תורה believes him even about the past. רבי יצחק בר ביסנא tries to prove this from the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים, but step 18 raises a new challenge, and step 19 ends with 'קשיא'.

phrases.english: If he were not believed,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁמַעְנֵיהּ נָמֵי לָא מְהֵימַן,
phrases.english: then even if we heard him, he would also not be believed,
because perhaps he said it only afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the push-back of Step 16 and brings back the proof of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the other way of knowing (hearing him) still needs us to believe him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might know about the פיגול just from hearing him, so there is no need to believe his later claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hearing him does not tell us when he spoke, so we must believe him anyway. The proof that the תורה believes him stands.

steps.title: Maybe they saw the כהן גדול through a small opening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again on the proof from the כהן גדול. Maybe people saw what he did through a small door.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe we saw him through a small door?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק בר ביסנא's proof one more time. Maybe people watched the כהן גדול through a small opening and saw him do the service wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needed the כהן גדול to be totally alone, so that only his own word could tell us about the פיגול. If people could watch him through a small door, then we know about the mistake from them. In that case the case says nothing about believing a person about himself.

phrases.english: But perhaps we saw him through a small door?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The answer in step 17 dealt with hearing the כהן גדול. This step offers a new way we might know about the פיגול: by seeing it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יצחק בר ביסנא's whole proof from the כהן גדול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes nobody could see the כהן גדול. A small opening would let witnesses see the mistake, so we would not need to believe him.

steps.title: The proof is left with a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer. The proof from the כהן גדול is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'קשיא'. The push-back from step 18 stands, and the proof from the כהן גדול falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no answer to the idea of the small opening, so this proof does not hold. This does not prove that רבי אסי's teaching is wrong. It only means this source cannot be used to support it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question stays unanswered.

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here is not a new question. It is the גמרא admitting that the last challenge has no answer, so the proof falls.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the push-back in step 18 cannot be answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא's proof from the כהן גדול is refuted.

steps.title: A סופר admits he wrote the names of ה' without proper intention
steps.stepSummary: A סופר comes to רבי אמי and says that, in a ספר תורה he wrote for someone, he did not write the אזכרות לשמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבי אמי and said: in the ספר תורה I wrote for so-and-so, I did not write the names of ה' with the proper intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a person who tells us about his own hidden mistake. This sets up רבי אמי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a סופר wrote ה''s names with the right intention is something only he knows. It is like the earlier cases, where a person says he did something wrong that nobody else could see.

keyTerms.meaning: The places where ה''s name is written

phrases.english: There was a certain man who came before Rabbi Ami;

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לִפְלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: he said to him: the Torah scroll that I wrote for so-and-so —
its mentions of God's name, I did not write them with the proper intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case on the same theme: a person who reports his own hidden mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a סופר says he wrote the אזכרות without proper intention.

steps.title: רבי אמי asks who has the scroll
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks whose hands the ספר תורה is in now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: whose hands is the ספר תורה in?
steps.whatsHappening: Before ruling, רבי אמי asks a clarifying question: where is the scroll right now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matters because it tells us whose loss is at stake. If the scroll already belongs to someone else, the סופר's words would hurt another person, not just himself.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בְּיַד מִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: the Torah scroll is in whose possession?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the facts of the case brought in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who currently holds the ספר תורה.

steps.title: The scroll is with the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The סופר answers that the ספר תורה is already with the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: in the buyer's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The סופר answers רבי אמי: the scroll has already been handed over to the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the scroll now belongs to someone else. The סופר's claim would cause a loss to the buyer, and that sets up the ruling.

phrases.english: He said to him: in the buyer's possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scroll is with the buyer.

steps.title: Believed to lose his pay, not to ruin the scroll
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that the סופר is believed about losing his own pay, but not about making the ספר תורה פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: you are believed to lose your own pay, but you are not believed to ruin the ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives his ruling. The סופר's words count against himself, but not against the scroll that now belongs to the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling splits the סופר's words in two. As an admission about himself, they cost him his pay. As a claim that would make the buyer's scroll פסול, they are not accepted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next two questions: how much pay does he lose, and why can't the scroll simply be fixed?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לְהַפְסִיד שְׂכָרְךָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: you are believed to make yourself lose your wage,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה נֶאֱמָן לְהַפְסִיד סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: but you are not believed to cause a loss to the Torah scroll.
phrases.notes: This means making it פסול, which would hurt the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling now that the facts are clear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סופר loses his pay, but the ספר תורה is not made פסול because of his words.

steps.title: Why lose pay for the whole scroll?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: fine, he loses pay for the names, but why lose pay for the whole ספר תורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: granted that he loses the pay for the names of ה'. Does he lose the pay for the whole ספר תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי אמי. The mistake was only in the names of ה', so why should the סופר lose pay for the rest of the scroll?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything except the names was written properly. So it would seem fair to take away only the pay for the names, not the pay for all his work.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him:
granted that he lost the wage for the mentions of God's name,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכַר דְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה כּוּלֵּיהּ מִי הִפְסִיד?!
phrases.english: did he lose the wage of the entire Torah scroll?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how much pay the ruling in step 23 takes away.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's ruling that the סופר loses his pay.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the names were written wrong, so only the pay for the names should be lost.

steps.title: Such a scroll is worth nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers yes: a ספר תורה whose names were not written לשמן is worth nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: yes, because any ספר תורה whose names of ה' were not written with proper intention is worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי defends his ruling. The סופר loses all his pay, because the whole scroll has no value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The names are not a small, separate part. A scroll without proper names cannot be used as a ספר תורה, so the buyer received nothing of value. That is why no pay at all is owed.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
because any Torah scroll
whose mentions of God's name are not written with proper intention
is not worth anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, שֶׁכׇּל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵין אַזְכָּרוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ כְּתוּבוֹת לִשְׁמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the facts: the loss covers the whole scroll.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bad names are only one part of the scroll, so only that part of the pay is lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without proper names the whole scroll is worth nothing, so all the pay is lost.

steps.title: Why not go over the names with a quill?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סופר can't just trace over the names with a quill and make them holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him pass a quill over them and make them holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that the scroll is worthless. Why not fix it by going over each name with the right intention?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the names could be fixed by writing over them לשמן, the scroll would be worth something after all. Then the סופר should not lose all his pay.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him make it holy

phrases.english: But let him pass a quill over them,
and sanctify it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's answer that the scroll is worth nothing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a scroll with names not written לשמן is worth nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The names can be fixed by going over them, so the scroll still has value.

steps.title: Is this ruling against רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this ruling follows, and suggests it may not match רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? Shall we say it is not like רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא's view the ruling follows, since it doesn't allow the quill fix. It suggests that the ruling goes against רבי יהודה. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the scroll is worthless means tracing over the names does not help. The גמרא suspects this does not fit רבי יהודה's view, which the next lines will discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view is being checked

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
Shall we say that it is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 26: since the quill fix is not allowed, the גמרא asks whose opinion that is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the ruling follows, and whether it goes against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי יהודה allows tracing over a name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A סופר meant to write יהודה but left out the ד, so the letters spell ה''s name. רבי יהודה says he may trace over it with a quill and make it holy. The חכמים say such a name is not the best quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A סופר needed to write the name of ה'. He meant to write 'יהודה' but made a mistake and left out the ד. He passes a quill over it and makes it holy. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: the name is not of the best quality.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its question from the last step. רבי יהודה holds that tracing over a name can make it holy, so רבי אמי's ruling seems to go against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said the whole ספר תורה is worthless when the names were not written לשמן. He never offered the fix of tracing over them. Since רבי יהודה allows that fix, רבי אמי's ruling seems to match only the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (introduces a quoted source)
Passes over it (traces on top of the letters)
Of the best or choicest quality

phrases.english: As we learned: If he needed
to write the Name of God;
and he intended to write 'Yehuda',
and he erred and did not put a dalet in it;
phrases.notes: Take the ד out of יהודה and you get God's name. So the right letters ended up on the page, just without the right intention.

phrases.english: he passes a quill over it and sanctifies it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
the Name is not of the choicest quality.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה צָרִיךְ לִכְתּוֹב אֶת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind step 27's suggestion that רבי אמי does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that רבי אמי's ruling (a ספר תורה with names not written לשמן is worthless) follows the חכמים and not רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי יהודה allows tracing over a name with a quill and the חכמים say it is not the best.

steps.title: Tracing one name is fine, but not a whole scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי can fit even רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה allowed tracing only for one name. Tracing every name in a whole ספר תורה would make it look blotchy.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only said this about one mention of the name. For a whole ספר תורה, no, because it would look speckled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and shows that רבי אמי does not have to argue with רבי יהודה. The two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tracing over one name is a small fix and looks normal. If every name in the scroll were traced, all the names would be darker and thicker than the rest of the writing. The scroll would look blotchy, so the fix does not work for a whole ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the ruling fits this opinion too)
He only said this as far as here (limits an opinion to its case)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's ruling works even for רבי יהודה. Tracing is a fix for one name, not for every name in the scroll, because that would look blotchy.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda –

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said his ruling
about a single mention of the Name,
but for the names of an entire Torah scroll – no,
because it would look speckled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in steps 27-28 by limiting רבי יהודה's ruling to one name.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (one name versus a whole scroll)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי's ruling must go against רבי יהודה, who allows tracing over a name.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יהודה allows tracing only for a single name. A whole scroll of traced names looks blotchy, so רבי אמי's ruling fits everyone.

steps.title: A סופר admits the parchment was not prepared לשמה
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. A סופר comes to רבי אבהו and says that the ספר תורה he wrote for someone was written on parchment he did not prepare לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבי אבהו and said to him: The ספר תורה I wrote for so-and-so, I did not prepare its parchment for its holy purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new case that is like רבי אמי's case. This step sets out the facts before רבי אבהו responds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the problem is not the names. It is the parchment, which has to be prepared לשמה. Just like in רבי אמי's case, a סופר is admitting something that would make the ספר תורה unusable.

keyTerms.meaning: Parchment sheets for a ספר תורה
For their holy purpose (with the right intention)

phrases.english: A certain man came before Rabbi Abbahu,
he said to him: The Torah scroll
that I wrote for so-and-so,
I did not process its parchment for its sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case that is like רבי אמי's ruling in step 23, this time about the parchment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: a סופר admits he did not prepare the parchment of a ספר תורה he sold לשמה.

steps.title: רבי אבהו asks who has the scroll
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks the סופר who has the ספר תורה right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The ספר תורה is in whose hands?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו asks one fact before he rules. The question sets up the answer and the ruling that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question shows that who holds the scroll matters to his ruling. The text does not say why yet. It only shows that he needs this fact before he decides.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בְּיַד מִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: The Torah scroll is in whose possession?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אבהו responds to the סופר's admission by asking for a key fact.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who currently holds the ספר תורה.

steps.title: The buyer has the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The סופר answers that the buyer has the ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In the hands of the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The סופר answers that the scroll is no longer with him. The buyer has it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי אבהו knows the scroll already belongs to the buyer. With this fact he is ready to give his ruling in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: In the possession of the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבהו's question from step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ספר תורה is with the buyer.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the סופר is believed to make the scroll unusable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rules that since the סופר is believed to lose his own pay, he is also believed to make the ספר תורה unusable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since you are believed to lose your pay, you are believed to make the ספר תורה lose its value.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives his ruling. The סופר's word counts both for losing his pay and for making the ספר תורה unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a מתוך argument: if we believe you about one thing, we believe you about the connected thing too. This goes further than רבי אמי in step 23. רבי אמי believed the סופר only about his pay and not about making the scroll פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (because you are believed about this, you are believed about that)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבי אמי in step 23. רבי אמי said the סופר is NOT believed to make the ספר תורה פסול. Here רבי אבהו says he IS believed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two ways of ruling on how far a סופר's own admission can go. The ספר תורה is already with the buyer, yet the סופר's word still makes it unusable.

phrases.english: He said to him: Since you are believed
to lose your wage,
you are believed to cause a loss to the Torah scroll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אבהו's ruling after learning that the buyer has the scroll.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אבהו holds that the סופר is believed both to lose his pay and to make the ספר תורה unusable. This differs from רבי אמי's ruling.
